 About these data 
 About our data
 This site was created and is being maintained by a small passionate team of earth scientists enthusiastic about volcanism and earthquakes. Our goal is to present you with the best available quake data.
 No single seismic network is able to monitor all quakes that occur in the world. This is why we continuously collect, aggregate, and compare earthquake data from more than 50 international and national data centers around the world in near real time. In addition, we analyze user-generated shaking reports to detect many earthquakes in areas with poor instrumental coverage or detect quakes even before they are published by monitoring agencies.
Our database is one of the most up to date and complete in the world. It currently contains data for about 10 million earthquakes since 1900. The AllQuakes website and Volcanoes&Earthquakes App both provide a way to visualize and analyze seismic events in near real time. You can browse current and past earthquakes for the whole world , or specific countries, regions or areas you define yourself . You will find extensive lists with links to details for each event, statistics , and interactive maps.

 Lam Dong Earthquake FAQ
 + When was the latest earthquake in Lam Dong?
 The last earthquake in Lam Dong occurred 19 years ago and had a magnitude of 1.9: Mag.  1.9 earthquake Tinh Ba Ria-Vung Tau - Tinh Tuyen Quang , Vietnam - May 15, 2007 - A light magnitude 1.9 earthquake hit 32 km (20 mi) away from La Gi , Tinh Tuyen Quang ,   Vietnam , on Tue, May 15, 2007 at 02:39 GMT. The depth of the quake could not be determined, but is assumed to be shallow. The quake was not felt (or at least not reported so).
 + How many quakes were there in Lam Dong since 1900?
 There was one earthquake of magnitude 1.9 in or near Lam Dong since 1900.
 + What was the strongest quake in Lam Dong since 1900?
 The strongest earthquake in Lam Dong since 1900 had a magnitude of 1.9 and occurred 19 years ago: Mag.  1.9 earthquake Tinh Ba Ria-Vung Tau - Tinh Tuyen Quang , Vietnam - May 15, 2007 - A light magnitude 1.9 earthquake hit 32 km (20 mi) away from La Gi , Tinh Tuyen Quang ,   Vietnam , on Tue, May 15, 2007 at 02:39 GMT. The depth of the quake could not be determined, but is assumed to be shallow. The quake was not felt (or at least not reported so).
